exposure: Mode of operative delivery (forceps, vacuum, cesarean)
outcome: Maternal adverse outcome composite (postpartum hemorrhage, transfusion, endometritis, peripartum hysterectomy, or intensive care unit admission)
Neonatal adverse outcome composite (5-minute Apgar score less than 4, respiratory morbidity, neonatal intensive care unit admission, shoulder dystocia, birth trauma, or sepsis)
cohort: Women carrying singleton fetuses at 37 weeks of gestation or greater who underwent attempted operative vaginal delivery or cesarean delivery from a low station in the second stage of labor (n=2,518)
finding: A trial of forceps delivery from a low station compared with cesarean delivery was associated with decreased neonatal morbidity among neonates born to nulliparous women, but no significant differences were found in maternal outcomes.
mod_finding: For nulliparous women, attempted forceps delivery was associated with a lower neonatal adverse outcome composite compared to cesarean delivery, while attempted vacuum delivery was not.
